explanation: The full offline reference completed successfully (exit 0, ~5 s, ~430 MiB peak RSS) on Python 3.13 with bioframe==0.8.0, matplotlib==3.11.2, numpy==2.5.4 and pandas==3.1.0 installed by the controller from the declared pyproject. The staging recipe recreated all three inputs from their original URLs with verified identity: ENCFF401MQL.bed.gz (649,474 bytes, md5 9dabac96e36309ed65dc1cb289c51079, matching the provider md5) and ENCFF356LFX.bed.gz (8,211 bytes, md5 393688b4f06c9ce26165d47433dd8c37, matching) from ENCODE, and JASPAR MA0139.1.tsv.gz (7,698,065 bytes, sha256 b1bbdac3...) from the UBC JASPAR mirror; the controller verified the staged files remained byte-identical after the offline run. Content checks confirmed the notebook's parsing assumptions against the staged bytes: the ENCODE peak file is a headerless 10-column BED6+4 table (40,587 records), the blacklist is headerless 3-column BED (910 records), and the JASPAR track has exactly one leading header line (zcat shows 'chr1 10470 10489 ...' as line 1) so the source's skiprows=1 is supported, yielding 770,049 7-column motif records with no all-NA columns. Both declared artifacts were produced: peaks_with_strongest_motif_blacklist_filtered.csv (40,557 data rows plus header) and motifs_per_peak.csv (40,587 counts, one per peak), consistent with the 40,587 input peaks. Two pandas-3 warnings surfaced for the source's chained-inplace operations; both were smoke-tested as no-ops that only emit warnings, not errors, so the computations completed under the library's own semantics without modifying the source.
source_adaptations: Replaced the three remote input URLs in analysis.py with local staged paths (/inputs/ENCFF401MQL.bed.gz, /inputs/ENCFF356LFX.bed.gz, and /inputs/ for jaspar_url) so the otherwise unchanged script reads the same bytes offline; the files are staged verbatim by stage-inputs.sh with md5/size verification against the preparation-recorded provenance.
No analysis-logic changes: all filtering, renaming, overlap/subtract operations, plotting calls, and parameters are preserved from the unmodified original.py.
unresolved_assumptions: The pandas 3.x chained-assignment warnings from the source's inplace replace and inplace rename calls were verified as no-ops under this pandas version (warnings, not errors); the resulting export reflects the source code executing unmodified under its installed pandas semantics, which may differ cosmetically (e.g., pval_2 kept as the -1 sentinel instead of being replaced with NaN) from an older-pandas execution, but the idxmax strongest-motif selection is unaffected since -1 is below all real pvals.

The JASPAR MA0139.1.tsv.gz download has no provider-recorded checksum in the provenance metadata, so it is verified only by exact byte size and sha256 recorded at staging; the one-header-line structure and motif schema were confirmed by direct inspection of the staged file.
